column1: # Parent-typed name vs the name printed on the document, and whether they are
# WRITTEN FROM NAMES, NOT FROM THE NORMALISER. CLAUDE.md is explicit that a
# corpus derived from the rule it tests is testing itself, and three instruments
# in this repo have already been caught doing exactly that. Every row here is a
# way a parent plausibly types their name against a way a document plausibly
# prints it — the rules were then made to fit, not the other way round.

column4: TN initial is the father's name, not a middle name
same, written the other way round
diacritics survive in one rendering only
honorific typed, absent on the ID
Md is Mohammad, a name — must not be stripped as a title
leading initial plus two given names
apostrophe present in one rendering only
married name differs from the ID — parent must correct it
single initial must not act as a wildcard
subset rule is symmetric: a maiden name absent from the ID still matches
one document token must not satisfy two typed ones
honorific alone leaves no tokens at all
